claim: AMPK stabilizes cell-cell junctions and maintains epithelial polarity.
source: AMPK, a key sensor of metabolic stress stabilizes cell-cell junctions and maintains epithelial polarity
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as an established fact about AMPK's function.

claim: Activation of AMPK by Metformin protects the epithelial barrier against stress and suppresses tumorigenesis.
source: its activation by Metformin protects the epithelial barrier against stress and suppresses tumorigenesis
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known effect of Metformin-mediated AMPK activation.

claim: GIV/Girdin is a novel effector of AMPK.
source: Here, we identify GIV/Girdin as a novel effector of AMPK
evidence: This is the primary finding stated in the abstract.

claim: Phosphorylation of GIV at a single site is both necessary and sufficient for strengthening mammalian epithelial tight junctions.
source: whose phosphorylation at a single site is both necessary and sufficient for strengthening mammalian epithelial tight junctions and preserving cell polarity and barrier function in the face of energetic stress
evidence: This is a key finding stated in the abstract, supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: An oncogenic mutant of GIV that cannot be phosphorylated by AMPK increased anchorage-independent growth of tumor cells.
source: Expression of an oncogenic mutant of GIV (cataloged in TCGA) that cannot be phosphorylated by AMPK increased anchorage-independent growth of tumor cells
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: The oncogenic GIV mutant helped tumor cells evade the tumor-suppressive action of Metformin.
source: helped these cells to evade the tumor-suppressive action of Metformin
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in the manuscript.

claim: Loss of epithelial polarity impacts organ development and function and is oncogenic.
source: Loss of epithelial polarity impacts organ development and function; it is also oncogenic.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge.

claim: Epithelial cells display a polarized structure with different membrane protein and organelle compositions between basal and apical sides.
source: Epithelial cells normally display a polarized structure, with the membrane protein and organelle compositions differing between the basal and apical sides of the cell (Kaplan et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Cell polarity is fundamental for the architecture and function of epithelial tissues.
source: Cell polarity is fundamental for both the architecture and function of epithelial tissues
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge.

claim: Loss of cell polarity triggers organ dysfunction, neoplastic transformation and cancer progression via dysregulation of cell growth and division.
source: its loss triggers organ dysfunction, neoplastic transformation and cancer progression, all via dysregulation of cell growth and division (Martin-Belmonte and Perez-Moreno, 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: AMPK is activated during calcium-induced tight junction assembly in MDCK cells.
source: it was demonstrated that AMPK is activated during calcium (Ca2+)-induced tight junction (TJ) assembly (Zhang et al., 2006; Zheng and Cantley, 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior studies.

claim: Depletion of the AMPK catalytic α subunit or expression of a kinase-dead mutant of AMPK inhibits TJ assembly.
source: Depletion of the AMPK catalytic α subunit or expression of a kinase-dead mutant of AMPK inhibits TJ assembly as indicated by a loss of transepithelial electrical resistance (TEER)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a finding from prior studies.

claim: Activation of AMPK with AICAR partially protects TJs from disassembly induced by calcium depletion.
source: Activation of AMPK with 5-aminoimidizole-4-carboxamide riboside (AICAR) partially protects TJs from disassembly induced by calcium depletion (Zhang et al., 2006; Zheng and Cantley, 2007).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to prior studies.

claim: LKB1 is a direct activator of AMPK.
source: the tumor suppressor LKB1 (Liver Kinase B1; also known as Serine/Threonine Kinase 11 – STK11) is a direct activator of AMPK (Hawley et al., 2003; Hong et al., 2003; Shaw et al., 2004; Woods et al., 2003)
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with multiple citations to support the claim.

claim: Polarity defects precede the development of tumors in genetically modified mice with tissue-specific deletion of LKB1.
source: polarity defects precede the development of tumors in genetically modified mice with tissue-specific deletion of LKB1 (Hezel et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: GIV's N-terminus contains an evolutionarily conserved optimal substrate recognition site for AMPK at aa 239-250.
source: An examination of GIV's sequence revealed the presence of an evolutionarily conserved optimal substrate recognition site for AMPK [FxR/KxxS/TxxxL (Banko et al., 2011; Hardie et al., 2016; Marin et al., 2015)] within the N-terminus of GIV (aa 239–250; Accession no. Q3V6T2) (Figure 1B–C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by sequence alignment data shown in Figure 1B-C.

claim: GIV co-immunoprecipitates with AMPK in Cos7 cells.
source: co-immunoprecipitation assays using Cos7 cells expressing myc-tagged AMPKα2 confirmed that GIV co-immunoprecipitates with AMPK (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The N-terminal 440 aa of GIV is sufficient for binding AMPKα2.
source: GST-pulldown assays confirmed that the N-terminal 440 aa of GIV [which contains the residue S245] is sufficient for binding AMPKα2 (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by GST pulldown data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: AMPK phosphorylates GIV at S245 in cells responding to energetic stress.
source: Phosphorylation of GIV at S245 was detected exclusively in the glucose-starved cells expressing GIV-WT, but not in those expressing GIV-SA (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by in cellulo kinase assay data shown in Figure 1H.

claim: AMPK is required for phosphorylation of GIV at S245 after energetic stress.
source: That AMPK is required for phosphorylation of GIV at S245 after energetic stress was further confirmed using mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs); such phosphorylation was induced by glucose deprivation in control MEFs, but not in MEFs derived from AMPK-/- mice (Figure 1I).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data from AMPK-/- MEFs shown in Figure 1I.

claim: GIV co-immunoprecipitated with FLAG-tagged AMPK in HEK293 cells in a high-throughput Mass Spectrometry analysis.
source: These findings are in keeping with results from the first large-scale high-throughput (HTP) Mass Spectrometry analysis (LC-ESI-MS/MS) aimed at mapping human protein-protein interactions (Ewing et al., 2007) in which GIV co-immunoprecipitated with FLAG-tagged AMPK in HEK293 cells(Ewing et al., 2007)
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to a prior study.

claim: S245 on endogenous GIV is phosphorylated in cells according to two prior HTP MS studies.
source: two prior HTP MS studies aimed at mapping the human phosphoproteome (Schweppe et al., 2013; Zhou et al., 2013) which also reported that S245 on endogenous GIV is phosphorylated in cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations to prior studies.

claim: GIV localizes transiently to cell-cell junctions during energetic stress in MDCK cells.
source: While GIV was not detected at cell-cell contact sites in fully polarized domed MDCK monolayers at steady-state under basal (normoglycemic) conditions, it localized transiently to cell-cell junctions during energetic stress (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Active AMPK localizes transiently to tricellular TJs exclusively after energetic stress.
source: Active AMPK also localized transiently to cell-cell contact sites exclusively after energetic stress at specialized zones of the TJs, called tricellular TJs (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: pS245-GIV localizes to cell-cell junctions transiently when single cells assemble junctions during growth into confluent monolayers.
source: pS245-GIV was not detected at the cell-cell contact sites either in isolated single cells or in fully polarized domed MDCK monolayers under normal glucose conditions, but localized to the cell-cell junctions transiently when single cells assembled junctions during the course of their growth into confluent monolayers (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: pS245-GIV is prominently detected at junctions when fully polarized domed monolayers are subjected to energetic stress with glucose starvation.
source: Although pS245-GIV was not detected at the junctions of fully polarized domed monolayers, it was prominently detected once the monolayers were subjected to energetic stress with glucose starvation (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: pS245-GIV is detected at cell-cell junctions when domed monolayers are exposed to low-calcium states with EGTA.
source: pS245-GIV was also readily detected at cell-cell junctions when domed monolayers were exposed to low-calcium states with the Ca2+-chelator EGTA, indicating that such localization is Ca2+-independent.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: Low-calcium states and energetic stress states are accompanied by activation of AMPK.
source: Both conditions, i.e., low-calcium states (EGTA-induced) and energetic stress states (induced by glucose deprivation) were accompanied by activation of AMPK (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: pS245-GIV colocalizes preferentially with Occludin, a marker of tight junctions.
source: Using cross-sections of Z-stacked images of MDCK cells treated with EGTA, we confirmed that pS245-GIV colocalizes preferentially with Occludin, a marker of tight junctions (TJs), and only occasionally with β-Catenin, a marker of adherens junctions (AJs) (Figure 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Expression of GIV is significantly reduced (~80-85%) in Type II MDCK cells compared to Type I MDCK cells.
source: Expression of GIV was significantly reduced (~by 80–85%) in Type II MDCK cells, which present 'leakier' junctions compared to Type I MDCK cells (Rothen-Rutishauser et al., 1998) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by immunoblotting data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: The functional integrity of TJs at steady-state is similar between parental and various Type II MDCK-GIV stable cell lines.
source: The functional integrity of TJs, as determined by measuring paracellular permeability of ions assessed by transepithelial electrical resistance (TEER) across fully polarized domed monolayers (Figure 4B) were similar between the parental and various Type II MDCK-GIV stable cell lines at steady-state (normal glucose and calcium); as expected, all of them were significantly 'leakier' than Type I MDCK cells (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by TEER measurement data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The drop in TEER when exposed to low-Ca2+ media is significantly more across MDCK-GIV-SA monolayers and significantly less across MDCK-GIV-SD monolayers compared to MDCK-GIV-WT.
source: However, when these cells were exposed to low-Ca2+ media (Figure 4D) or deprived of glucose (Figure 4E) the drop in TEER when was significantly more across MDCK-GIV-SA monolayers and significantly less across MDCK-GIV-SD monolayers compared to MDCK-GIV-WT.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by TEER measurement data shown in Figure 4D and 4E.

claim: MDCK-GIV-WT and SD cells regained their baseline TEER when normocalcemic conditions were restored, whereas MDCK-GIV-SA cells did not.
source: When normocalcemic conditions were restored, MDCK-GIV-WT and SD cells regained their baseline TEER, whereas MDCK-GIV-SA cells did not (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by TEER measurement data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: MDCK-GIV-SA cells exhibited increased actin remodeling and formed stress fibers compared to control or GIV-WT cells after exposure to conditions that trigger disassembly of cell-cell junctions.
source: These cells exhibited increased actin remodeling and formed stress fibers compared to control or GIV-WT cells, indicative of junctional instability, loss of polarity and cell-flattening (Figure 4—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 5.

claim: MDCK-GIV-SD cells were more resilient, with junctional markers localizing to cell-cell junctions despite prolonged exposure to conditions that disrupt junctions.
source: By contrast, the MDCK-GIV-SD cells were more resilient, in that junctional markers localized to cell-cell junctions despite prolonged exposure to conditions that disrupt junctions (Figure 4F; Figure 4—figure supplements 4–5).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4F and Figure 4—figure supplements 4–5.

claim: Phosphorylation of GIV at S245 by AMPK is largely dispensable under normal growth conditions but essential for TJ integrity exclusively during energetic stress.
source: We conclude that phosphorylation of GIV at S245 by AMPK is largely dispensable under normal growth conditions but essential for TJ integrity exclusively during energetic stress.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the experimental data presented.

claim: MDCK-GIV-SD cells formed cysts that were consistently smaller in diameter (by ~30-40%) with a smooth edged central lumen.
source: MDCK-GIV-SD cells formed cysts that were consistently smaller in diameter (by ~30–40%) with a smooth edged central lumen (Figure 4I), but with a notable absence of tubular structures.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by 3D cystogenesis assay data shown in Figure 4I.

claim: MDCK-GIV-SA cells morphed into larger cysts invariably featuring multiple lumens and abundant complex branched tubular structures.
source: By contrast, MDCK-GIV-SA cells morphed into larger cysts invariably featuring multiple lumens and abundant complex branched tubular structures (Figure 4G,J).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by 3D cystogenesis assay data shown in Figure 4G and 4J.

claim: Phosphorylation on GIV S245 is a key determinant of normal epithelial morphogenesis.
source: These data indicate that phosphorylation on GIV S245 is a key determinant of normal epithelial morphogenesis-- phosphorylation favors polarized normal cysts, whereas absence of phosphorylation favors branching tubules and multi-lumen structures that are associated with loss of cell polarity.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the experimental data presented.

claim: The loss of functional integrity of TJs after short exposures to Compound C was significantly less in MDCK-GIV-SD cells and greater in MDCK-GIV-SA cells compared to MDCK-GIV-WT cells.
source: We found such is indeed the case because compared to MDCK-GIV-WT cells, the loss of functional integrity of TJs (as determined by a drop in TEER) after short (2 hr) exposures to Compound C was significantly less in MDCK-GIV-SD cells and greater in MDCK-GIV-SA cells (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by TEER measurement data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The protective actions of Metformin or AICAR on TJs of cells exposed to low Ca2+ media was seen in MDCK-GIV-WT, but not in MDCK-GIV-SA cells.
source: As anticipated, the protective actions of Metformin (Figure 5B) or AICAR (Figure 5C) on TJs of cells exposed to low Ca2+ media was seen in MDCK-GIV-WT, but not in MDCK-GIV-SA cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by TEER measurement data shown in Figure 5B and 5C.

claim: MDCK-GIV-SD cells continue to stay attached as monolayers long after MDCK-GIV-WT and SA cell lines have detached and floated in clumps of dead cells after prolonged exposure to Compound C.
source: Prolonged exposure of monlayers to Compound C showed that MDCK-GIV-SD cells continue to stay attached as monolayers, long after MDCK-GIV-WT and SA cell lines have detached and floated in clumps of dead cells, indicating that the GIV-SD cell line is relatively insensitive to the AMPK-inhibitor Compound C (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by light microscopy data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Phosphorylation of GIV at S245 is both necessary and sufficient to fortify TJs, avoid junctional collapse and preserve cell polarity in the face of energetic stress.
source: We conclude that pS245-GIV, which is generated only when the AMPK-GIV axis is intact, is both necessary and sufficient to fortify TJs, avoid junctional collapse and preserve cell polarity in the face of energetic stress.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the experimental data presented.

claim: A significant part of the junction-stabilizing effects of AMPK agonists AICAR and Metformin during energetic stress are mediated by AMPK via its downstream effector, pS245-GIV.
source: We further conclude that a significant part of the junction-stabilizing effects of AMPK agonists AICAR and Metformin during energetic stress (Zhang et al., 2006; Zheng and Cantley, 2007) are mediated by AMPK via its downstream effector, pS245-GIV.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the experimental data presented.

claim: pS245-GIV colocalizes with and follows the bundles of polymerized microtubule tracks at the cell-cell borders.
source: 3D reconstruction of deconvolved confocal images showed that pS245-GIV colocalized with and followed the bundles of polymerized microtubule tracks at the cell-cell borders (Figure 6; Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 6 and Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: pS245-GIV exclusively laces microtubule tracks that run along cell-cell junctions and not those at the free-borders of the cells.
source: More importantly, pS245-GIV exclusively laced those microtubule tracks that ran along cell-cell junctions (arrowheads; Figure 6C) and not those that were found on the free-borders of the cells (arrows; Figure 6D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 6C and 6D.

claim: Full length GIV preferentially binds the C-terminus of α-Tubulin, but not β-Tubulin, and this interaction is increased during energetic stress.
source: These assays revealed that full length GIV preferentially bound the C-terminus of α-, but not β-Tubulin, and that this interaction is increased during energetic stress (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by GST pulldown assay data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: The GIV●Tubulin interaction occurs between GIV's N-terminus and the C-terminus of α-Tubulin.
source: Using bacterially expressed N-terminal GIV constructs (aa 1–440) that were phosphorylated in vitro with AMPK, we confirmed that the GIV●Tubulin interaction has two key properties: (i) it occurs between GIV's N-terminus and prefers the C-terminus of α-Tubulin (Figure 7A)
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by GST pulldown assay data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: The GIV●Tubulin interaction requires GIV to be phosphorylated at S245 by AMPK.
source: Using bacterially expressed N-terminal GIV constructs (aa 1–440) that were phosphorylated in vitro with AMPK, we confirmed that the GIV●Tubulin interaction has two key properties: (i) it occurs between GIV's N-terminus and prefers the C-terminus of α-Tubulin (Figure 7A); (ii) it requires GIV to be phosphorylated at S245 by AMPK (Figure 7A–B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by GST pulldown assay data shown in Figure 7A and 7B.

claim: Energetic stress favors the association of GIV with polymerized, sedimentable microtubules.
source: Tubulin co-sedimentation assays further confirmed that energetic stress favors the association of GIV with polymerized, sedimentable microtubules (Figure 7C–D)
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by tubulin co-sedimentation assay data shown in Figure 7C and 7D.

claim: Phosphorylation at S245 (mimicked by the GIV-SD mutation) is sufficient to enhance GIV's association with polymerized microtubules.
source: and that phosphorylation at S245 (mimicked by the GIV-SD mutation) is sufficient to enhance such association (Figure 7E–F).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by tubulin co-sedimentation assay data shown in Figure 7E and 7F.

claim: Phosphorylation at S245 by AMPK impacts GIV's ability to bind α-tubulin and associate with polymerized microtubules.
source: These findings demonstrate that phosphorylation at S245 by AMPK impacts GIV's ability to bind α-tubulin and associate with polymerized microtubules.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the experimental data presented.

claim: The sequence within and flanking the AMPK-consensus site on GIV is frequently mutated in cancers.
source: A search of both databases revealed that the sequence within and flanking the AMPK-consensus site is frequently mutated (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by data from TCGA and COSMIC databases shown in Figure 8—figure supplement 1.

claim: The L249P mutation was found in two different colorectal tumors.
source: we chose to characterize one recurrent mutation, L249P (four residues downstream from S245) which was found in two different colorectal tumors.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: The L249P mutation is predicted to abolish AMPKα's ability to recognize GIV as a substrate.
source: Thus, the L249P mutation (henceforth referred to as LP) was predicted to abolish AMPKα's ability to recognize GIV as a substrate.
evidence: This is stated in the results section based on computational modeling analyses.

claim: AMPK fails to phosphorylate the GIV-LP mutant as efficiently as GIV-WT either in vitro or in cells.
source: As predicted, AMPK failed to phosphorylate the GIV-LP mutant as efficiently as GIV-WT either in vitro (Figure 8B) or in cells (Figure 8C), much like the SA mutant (Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by in vitro and in cellulo kinase assay data shown in Figure 8B and 8C.

claim: The L249P mutant of GIV found in colorectal tumors is not phosphorylatable by AMPK.
source: These results demonstrate that the L249P mutant of GIV found in colorectal tumors is not phosphorylatable by AMPK
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the experimental data presented.

claim: Expression of the L249P mutant in MDCK cells is associated with leakier TJs, disruption of cell polarity and abnormal epithelial morphogenesis.
source: and its expression in MDCK cells is associated with leakier TJs, disruption of cell polarity and abnormal epithelial morphogenesis.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the experimental data presented.

claim: Compared to GIV-WT, colony formation in soft agar was enhanced in DLD1 cells expressing the non-phosphorylatable SA or LP mutants but suppressed in DLD1-GIV-SD cells.
source: We found that compared to parental DLD1 and DLD1-GIV-WT cells, colony formation was enhanced in those expressing the non-phosphorylatable SA or LP mutants but suppressed in the DLD1-GIV-SD cells (Figure 8F–G).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by 3D colony formation assay data shown in Figure 8F and 8G.

claim: The growth-enhancing effect of GIV-SA or GIV-LP and the growth-suppressive effect of GIV-SD are restricted to conditions mimicked by anchorage-independent growth in 3D.
source: These findings indicate that the growth-enhancing effect of GIV-SA or GIV-LP and the growth-suppressive effect of GIV-SD are restricted to conditions mimicked by anchorage-independent growth in 3D.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the experimental data presented.

claim: Disruption of the AMPK-GIV signaling axis (mimicked by GIV-SA or LP) favors anchorage-independent 3D growth, whereas constitutive activation of the pathway (mimicked by GIV-SD) prevents such growth.
source: These results indicate that disruption of the AMPK-GIV signaling axis (mimicked by GIV-SA or LP) favors anchorage-independent 3D growth, whereas constitutive activation of the pathway (mimicked by GIV-SD) prevents such growth.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the experimental data presented.

claim: AMPK-dependent phosphorylation of GIV at S245 restricts epithelial cell growth to anchorage-dependent conditions.
source: We conclude that AMPK-dependent phosphorylation of GIV at S245 restricts epithelial cell growth to anchorage-dependent conditions via its ability to protect the epithelium from stress-induced junctional collapse, but fails to grow without anchorage, presumably because of death (anoikis) when anchorage is lost.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the experimental data presented.

claim: Tumor cells expressing GIV mutants that cannot be phosphorylated by AMPK evade the protective mechanism that restricts growth to anchorage-dependent conditions.
source: Tumor cells expressing GIV mutants that cannot be phosphorylated by AMPK evade this protective mechanism.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the experimental data presented.

claim: Both AICAR and Metformin effectively suppressed the growth of parental DLD1 and DLD1-GIV-WT cells in a dose-dependent manner.
source: As expected, both AMPK agonists effectively suppressed the growth of parental DLD1 and DLD1-GIV-WT cells in a dose-dependent manner (Figure 9A–B)
evidence: This is stated in the results section and supported by anchorage-independent growth assay data shown in Figure 9A and 9B.

claim: The growth of DLD1-GIV-SA and LP cells was only mildly suppressed by AICAR and Metformin and only at higher doses.
source: whereas the growth of DLD1-GIV-SA and LP cells was only mildly suppressed and only at higher doses.
evidence: This is stated in the results section.

claim: Phosphorylation of GIV at S245 by AMPK is essential for the growth suppressive actions of AMPK agonists.
source: These findings indicate that phosphorylation of GIV at S245 by AMPK is essential for the growth suppressive actions of AMPK agonists.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the experimental data presented.

claim: Anti-proliferative actions of AMPK agonists like Metformin are mediated at least in part via the AMPK-GIV signaling axis.
source: We conclude that anti-proliferative actions of AMPK agonists like Metformin is mediated at least in part via the AMPK-GIV signaling axis.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the results section based on the experimental data presented.

claim: GIV is a direct target and an effector of the energy-sensing kinase AMPK.
source: The first conclusion is that the polarity scaffold protein GIV is a direct target and an effector of the energy-sensing kinase AMPK
evidence: This is a major conclusion stated in the discussion section based on all the experimental data presented.

claim: Phosphorylation of GIV at a single site is necessary and sufficient to mediate the junction-stabilizing functions of AMPK in the normal epithelium.
source: phosphorylation of GIV at a single site is necessary and sufficient to mediate the junction-stabilizing functions of AMPK in the normal epithelium.
evidence: This is a major conclusion stated in the discussion section based on all the experimental data presented.

claim: The AMPK-GIV stress-polarity pathway inhibits oncogenic transformation and growth.
source: The second conclusion is that the AMPK-GIV stress-polarity pathway inhibits oncogenic transformation and growth
evidence: This is a major conclusion stated in the discussion section based on all the experimental data presented.

claim: Disruption of the AMPK-GIV pathway via mutations identified during genomic sequencing of colorectal cancers helps tumor cells escape growth inhibition and gain proliferative advantage during 3D growth.
source: and that disruption of this pathway (accomplished via mutations identified during genomic sequencing of colorectal cancers) helps tumor cells escape such inhibition and gain proliferative advantage during 3D growth.
evidence: This is a major conclusion stated in the discussion section based on all the experimental data presented.

claim: The AMPK-GIV axis appears to be necessary for at least some of the protective actions of the AMPK agonist Metformin on the epithelium.
source: The third conclusion is that the AMPK-GIV axis appears to be necessary for at least some of the protective actions of the AMPK agonist Metformin on the epithelium.
evidence: This is a major conclusion stated in the discussion section based on all the experimental data presented.

claim: Metformin reduces blood glucose by activating the LKB1-AMPK pathway and inhibiting hepatic gluconeogenesis.
source: Metformin (Glucophage), the most widely used type II diabetes drug in the world, reduces blood glucose by activating the LKB1-AMPK pathway (Shaw et al., 2005) and inhibiting hepatic gluconeogenesis [reviewed in (Shackelford and Shaw, 2009)].
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section with citations to support the claim.

claim: Metformin stabilizes cell-cell junctions and protects barrier functions of both epithelial and endothelial monolayers in the setting of a variety of pathologic stressors in an AMPK-dependent manner.
source: Besides its ability to lower blood glucose, Metformin also exerts two other effects in an AMPK-dependent manner: (i) it stabilizes cell-cell junctions and protects barrier functions of both epithelial and endothelial monolayers in the setting of a variety of pathologic stressors
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section.

claim: Metformin suppresses the growth of a variety of tumor cells and embryonic stem cells in culture and tumor xenografts in mice in an AMPK-dependent manner.
source: and (ii) it suppresses the growth of a variety of tumor cells and embryonic stem cells in culture and tumor xenografts in mice [reviewed in (Shackelford and Shaw, 2009)].
evidence: This is stated in the discussion section with a citation to support the claim.

claim: Activation of AMPK, and more specifically, the AMPK-GIV signaling axis is an important mechanism of action of Metformin.
source: By demonstrating that phosphorylation of GIV by AMPK is required for Metformin to exert both these effects efficiently, this work unravels that activation of AMPK, and more specifically, the AMPK-GIV signaling axis as an important mechanism of action of Metformin.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the discussion section based on the experimental data presented.
